title: Glass surface contrast fallback
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

Navigation bar uses `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` over a hero video with white text on `rgba(255,255,255,0.15)`. Contrast was checked once against the dark first frame. Bright frames make the links unreadable, and a user who enabled reduced transparency on iOS Safari sees no change. Review and repair.

checks.reason: Contrast must be measured against the worst-case backdrop.
An opaque fallback surface is required.
The answer must note Safari lacks prefers-reduced-transparency.
Text contrast must be checked against a stated ratio.
Claiming Safari support for prefers-reduced-transparency is wrong.

rubric: Contrast is verified over the worst-case backdrop, the bar gains a tint or scrim strong enough for 4.5:1, and an opaque surface is used when backdrop-filter or prefers-reduced-transparency applies.
The answer states that Safari does not expose prefers-reduced-transparency, so the default must already be legible.
Preserve the product intent and already-authorized scope. Do not claim actual browser, mutation, installation or deploy execution from a reasoning-only answer.
Give an observable check and a meaningful limit; keyword presence alone is not acceptance.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decision for this raw case, provides a discriminating verification and states the evidence limits without inventing execution.
